title: SDK quirks and workarounds — tribe log (Mar 24, 2026)
summary: Mid-week sync capturing oddball SDK behaviours observed across quickstarts and samples. Not exhaustive — focused on recurrent flakiness and short-term mitigations we can ship this sprint.
notes:
Observed three classes of problems this week: (1) stream+retry race in typescript SDK when using continuous batching + prefix cache flush; (2) Python tokenizer edge case: surrogate pairs cause off-by-one token counts in embeddings quickstart; (3) quickstart Docker builds failing in musl-based alpine images (ffi/torch wheels mismatch).

Conversation highlights:
- Jonas walked through a repro of TS stream race: sequence of stream close + retry can double-invoke a fallback handler. Root hypothesis: overlapping socket.destroy() + setImmediate() reorder when network error triggers, causing duplicate callback invocation. Quick temp mitigation is idempotent handlers (see action item).
- Priya ran the Python quickstart on M1 dev kits and saw embedding token counts 1–2 tokens higher for emojis and some CJK sequences. Hypothesis: tokenization glue layer (rust-binding) version mismatch between vendored tokenizer in wheel vs local compiled lib. Workaround: pin tokenizer wheel to v0.8.2 or run fallback pure-Python tokenizer which matches production model. We'll run deterministic test vectors.
- Marisol flagged that some partner quickstarts (notably node-ssr-sample) fail CI in alpine images due to prebuilt wheels expecting glibc; local workaround is to use node:18-bullseye-slim or add cross-compile steps in Dockerfile. We should update quickstart README to recommended base images and add a CI matrix entry.

Misc notes:
- Samples repo linter started failing after license header enforcement; quick patch added in PR #842 but we need authoring guidance to avoid churn.
- Telemetry: current SDK telemetry doesn't capture 'retry-after' variant or prefix-cache-hit ratio; adding a short event will help correlate customer tickets with infra logs.

Decisions:
- Ship idempotent safety wrapper for TS streaming handlers this sprint (low risk).
- Add tokenizer pinned wheel to python-quickstart Dockerfile for M1 workflows and create test vectors.
- Update quickstart docs with recommended base images and CI test matrix.

open_questions: Is the TS stream race reproducible on all node versions or only on older 14/16 runtimes?
Can we standardize around a tokenizer wheel for mac M1 CI to avoid local compile variance?
Do we want to treat alpine CI as a 'must-pass' for quickstarts or mark as compatibility best-effort?

quick_patches: TS idempotent wrapper snippet: const safeInvoke = (fn) => { let called = false; return (...args) => { if (called) return; called = true; fn(...args); } }
Python Dockerfile pin: RUN pip install tokenizers==0.8.2 && pip install -r requirements.txt
Dockerfile note for node-ssr-sample: FROM node:18-bullseye-slim  # avoids musl wheel issues
